html:
At Reykjavík on 11 and 12 October 1986, the American president Ronald Reagan and the Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met at Höfði House and came close to agreeing to abolish all nuclear weapons.

Iceland was chosen as a neutral spot halfway between Washington and Moscow. The talks went far: deep cuts in missiles and even the end of nuclear arms were discussed. They broke down over Reagan's plan for missile defence in space.

The summit seemed a failure, but the trust and the proposals it produced led to the treaty of 1987 that removed a whole class of medium-range missiles from Europe. It is seen as a turning point towards the end of the Cold War. See Iceland.
